title: anthriscus sylvestris subsp. fumarioides
intro: Anthriscus sylvestris subsp. fumarioides, commonly known as wild chervil or wild celery, is a plant species within the carrot family, Apiaceae. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which can help to soothe digestive issues, reduce fever, and protect against cell damage. The therapeutic actions of wild chervil include its ability to relax the muscles, reduce anxiety, and promote sleep, as well as its use in treating respiratory issues such as bronchitis and coughs. The bioactive constituents of wild chervil include volatile oils, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and make it a valuable herb in traditional and modern medicine.
